principle: A nonexistent original is generated by fabricating the complete machinery of its recovery, where dense documented transmission substitutes for the source itself and the deliberately undocumented final link keeps the promised original permanently suspended beyond verification.

nodes.label: Found-manuscript frame with amputated recovery link
nodes.description: The narrative is presented as an edited translation of a recovered codex, with every internal transmission link documented except the final link to the modern editor, which is deliberately omitted so the frame terminates in a void.
evidence: The Prologue and Note on the Shire Records present the entire text as an edited translation of a recovered codex.
Unlike Otranto or Cide Hamete conventions, the chain from Middle-earth to the modern editor is never narrated.
Stage 4 finds the Red Book is this frame; remove it and no freestanding text remains beneath the device.
rules: every internal transmission boundary is documented except the terminal link
verification is permanently deferred one stratum beyond reach

nodes.label: Layered composite authorship
nodes.description: The text is attributed in dated strata to Bilbo, Frodo, Sam, and later scribes, with visible seams such as crossed-out titles and blank final leaves reserved for a successor hand, serializing authorship inside the fiction.
evidence: Explicit attribution of strata: Bilbo memoir, Frodo continuation, Sam additions, plus Bilbo volumes of Translations from the Elvish.
Diegetic composition scenes such as the title-page moment in The Grey Havens.
Stage 4 rates it central: serialized strata make this a codex rather than a generic frame-tale.
rules: eyewitness memoir contract limits admissible perspective

nodes.label: Translation-layer disguise
nodes.description: Appendix F declares the English surface a systematic substitution for invented source languages, with Westron rendered as English and Rohirric as Old English, so the reader is told the shown text is never the original.
evidence: Appendix F is a systematic declared specification of linguistic substitution, not an aside.
The subtraction test finds its removal collapses nomenclature logic and reduces the appendices to trivia.
The conceit certifies the manuscript reality at the cost of declaring every visible word a substitution.
rules: the surface text is a total substitution and never the original

nodes.label: Pseudo-editorial apparatus
nodes.description: Appendices A-F, dual calendar systems, genealogical tables, the Tale of Years, and translator footnotes form a scholarly armature attached to the narrative, supplying the checkable substrate the translation claim requires.
evidence: Appendices A-F, calendars, genealogies, and footnotes constitute a full visible scholarly armature.
Stage 4 notes co-dependence with the translation layer but judges the density partly substitutable; a thinner armature might suffice.
Removing the frame apparatus collapses calendar systems, nomenclature logic, and errata reconciliation.

nodes.label: Transmission stemma in the Note on the Shire Records
nodes.description: Specified copies and recensions including the Thains Book, Findegil's Minas Tirith copy, later interpolations, and annotations in multiple hands, simulating manuscript wear and variance as fabricated patina.
evidence: The Note on the Shire Records specifies copies, recensions, interpolations, and marginalia with scribal precision.
Stage 2 finds the density of documented links makes the single undocumented terminal link conspicuous.
Stage 4 rates it a high-confidence supporting mechanism that amplifies authentication.

nodes.label: Riddle-game errata absorbed as manuscript variance
nodes.description: The discrepancy between the 1937 and 1951 versions of the riddle-game chapter is reconciled diegetically: Bilbo's lie is recorded as the original entry and corrected in later recensions, converting real revision into fictional recension history.
evidence: Real-world revision history of The Hobbit is laundered into the fictional stemma as a documented variant.
Stage 2 identifies a mutually validating loop: the stemma creates the category of variance and the errata deposits a real instance into it.
Stage 4 calls it brilliant but opportunistic; the frame stands without it.

nodes.label: Title-page palimpsest of crossed-out titles
nodes.description: In The Grey Havens the manuscript title page displays successive crossed-out titles before Frodo's final one, rendering revision marks visible as seams between attributed strata.
evidence: Crossed-out serial titles from My Diary onward are shown before the final title.
Stage 2 notes the palimpsest is legible as revision history only because authorship is already serialized.
Stage 4 classes it incidental: a single-instance flourish since stratum boundaries are established by attribution elsewhere.

nodes.label: Blank final leaves reserved for Sam
nodes.description: Frodo leaves the final pages blank for Sam, making the manuscript's terminal boundary an open edge that reads as the next stratum awaiting deposit and enacts the theme of succession formally.
evidence: Frodo tells Sam the last pages are for him, leaving the codex structurally unfinished by design.
Stage 2 finds the open edge is the ending's mechanism, writing Frodo's departure into the codex as unwritten pages.
Stage 4 rates it supporting: the frame's identity survives its removal.
rules: the terminal boundary is left unwritten for a successor hand

nodes.label: Verse with English rhyme, meter, and wordplay
nodes.description: The poems operate by aesthetic self-sufficiency inside a system claiming total derivativeness; English rhyme and puns cannot be translations of Westron, so the frame must tolerate an element that contradicts it.
evidence: Stage 3 finds the verse refuses the translation logic: rhyme, meter, and puns cannot be renderings of a source language.
The refusal is load-bearing; stripping the verbal pleasure to honor the conceit would make the text fail as literature.
rule_violations: the surface text is a total substitution and never the original

nodes.label: Appendix B narrating past the blank leaves
nodes.description: The Tale of Years documents Sam's departure and the age's end within the same binding, closing elsewhere the open edge the blank leaves promise to hold open.
evidence: Stage 3 finds the codex simultaneously withholds and delivers its continuation: Appendix B narrates past the blank leaves.
The open-edge promise of unwritten succession is contradicted inside the same volume.
rule_violations: the terminal boundary is left unwritten for a successor hand

nodes.label: Scenes beyond any hobbit witness
nodes.description: The prose narrates Gollum's private deliberations, councils no hobbit attended, and Boromir's death from perspectives no attributed testimony could reach, systematically breaching the eyewitness memoir contract.
evidence: Stage 3 identifies systematic violation: private deliberations, unattended councils, and deaths without surviving witnesses.
The apparatus patches some breaches with debriefings and secondhand accounts but not all; the frame survives by not pressing its own standard.
rule_violations: eyewitness memoir contract limits admissible perspective

edges.rationale: The translation conceit requires the appendical apparatus to supply an original substrate; without the calendars, genealogies, and nomenclature tables the translation claim has no referent.
Each becomes inert without the other: remove the translation conceit and the appendices become trivia, since the apparatus only matters as the checkable substrate of a declared source language.
The amputated terminal link reads as active void only if all internal transmission links are documented with exhaustive scribal precision; the stemma supplies that documentation.
Errata absorption requires the transmission stemma to pre-establish the category of manuscript variance, otherwise the riddle-game reconciliation is an ad hoc patch.
The reconciliation deposits a real variant into the stemma's category of variance; without an actual instance to absorb, the stemma would be inert texture.

The title-page palimpsest carries load only because composite authorship already serializes the text into attributed strata; crossed-out titles are legible as revision history only against stratum boundaries.
The blank final leaves read as a successor stratum awaiting deposit rather than narrative failure only because composite authorship serializes the text into attributed layers.
A title page displaying successive hands establishes the precedent that permits the blank leaves to read as the next stratum rather than as failure; the leaves still function without it.

Producing the original would make the frame falsifiable, so the amputated terminal link supplies the warrant the translation claim trades on: authentication depends on verification being permanently deferred one stratum beyond reach.

Reliability is manufactured from documented unreliability: recording Bilbo's lie as the original entry validates the frame by convicting its own witness, offering the discrepancy as proof the manuscript exists.

If apparatus density decreases below narrative need, the frame reverts to decoration and the documented feel of the world degrades; the dense armature strengthens the frame but the frame survives thinner apparatus.
Serialized strata make the frame a specific codex rather than a generic frame-tale; under progressive stripping a generic frame survives the removal of composite authorship.

The eyewitness memoir contract limits admissible perspective, and every scene beyond hobbit testimony strains the frame it cannot fully patch; the violation is systematic and the frame survives by not enforcing its own standard.

If the translation claim is enforced on the verse, its rhyme, meter, and wordplay become impossible, so the frame must tolerate untranslated aesthetic self-sufficiency as a concealed load-bearing exception.
The open-edge promise of unwritten succession is contradicted by Appendix B, which narrates past the blank leaves within the same binding, closing the open edge elsewhere in the codex.

violated: eyewitness memoir contract limits admissible perspective

failure_modes.consequence: The memoir frame breaks whenever the prose narrates scenes no attributed witness could access, such as Gollum's private deliberations and deaths without survivors; the frame persists only by declining to enforce its own evidentiary standard.

violated: verification is permanently deferred one stratum beyond reach

failure_modes.consequence: The authentication loop is circular: every checkable claim terminates in fabricated evidence, so any demand to actually produce the original makes the frame falsifiable and collapses the entire authentication system.

violated: the surface text is a total substitution and never the original

failure_modes.consequence: The verse contradicts the total-derivativeness claim, since English rhyme and puns cannot be translations; enforcing the conceit destroys the verse as literature, so the frame must conceal a load-bearing exception rather than resolve it.

violated: the terminal boundary is left unwritten for a successor hand

failure_modes.consequence: The open-edge promise of unwritten succession is contradicted by Appendix B, which narrates past the blank leaves within the same binding; the codex simultaneously withholds and delivers its continuation.

Without the documented internal links, the amputated terminal link reads as mere omission rather than active void, and the riddle-game reconciliation reverts to an ad hoc patch; M1 loses coherence and the errata mechanism loses its category of variance.

The translation claim loses its checkable referent and becomes inert, and the documented feel of the world degrades; the frame reverts toward decoration with only a generic recovered-manuscript conceit and serialized authorship remaining.
Nomenclature logic collapses and the appendices reduce to trivia; the frame loses its claim to reality since the surface text is no longer certified as a mediated substitute for an unseen original.

Only a generic frame-tale remains: the title-page palimpsest and blank final leaves lose their stratum boundaries and cease to carry load, and the codex loses its identity as a serialized composite manuscript.

asserted_removal_tests.M1: If removed, no work remains at all, since there is no freestanding text beneath the frame device.
asserted_removal_tests.M2: If removed, the codex collapses into a generic frame-tale and the palimpsest, open-edge ending, and errata absorption lose their attachment points.
asserted_removal_tests.M3: If removed, the nomenclature logic collapses and the appendices become inert trivia with no original substrate to reference.
asserted_removal_tests.M4: If removed, the translation claim loses its referent and the fabricated provenance becomes an unverifiable assertion rather than a simulated evidence system.
